title: All domestic pigeon breeds descend from the rock-pigeon

fields.label: Label
fields.value: All domestic pigeon breeds descend from the rock-pigeon

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: All domestic pigeon breeds, however different, have descended from the rock-pigeon (Columba livia) and its geographical sub-species, not from several aboriginal wild stocks.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: I can feel no doubt that all our domestic breeds have descended from the Columba livia with its geographical sub-species.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter I, “Variation under Domestication”; section “Domestic Pigeons, their Differences and Origin”. Scope: domestic pigeon breeds

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch01-10: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.90

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The historical alternatives have direct genomic predictions and broad public sampling. Standard phylogenomics and ancestry inference can resolve the claim with high power.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare whole genomes of diverse domestic pigeon breeds with Columba livia subspecies and other candidate wild stocks using phylogenetic and admixture models. Nesting of all breeds within rock-pigeon diversity supports the claim; a distinct ancestral contribution would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Recent introgression must be distinguished from primary ancestry.

Some geographic wild populations remain undersampled.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.91
analysis feasibility: 0.85
operationalizability: 0.93
data adequacy: 0.82
data existence: 0.94

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The named ancestor and the alternative of several wild stocks are both directly readable from public pigeon and Columba sequences. Major breed groups and the rock-pigeon have already been deposited, so a reanalysis is weeks of standard phylogenomics rather than a new collecting program. Incomplete sampling of obscure breeds and wild subspecies limits certainty at the margin and does not block a confirm-or-refute test of the stated origin.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Place domestic pigeon breeds and wild Columba species, including geographical forms of Columba livia, on a multilocus tree and an admixture graph. Nesting of all breed groups inside C. livia would support single origin from the rock-pigeon; breed groups scattered among other wild Columba species would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Feral pigeons and later hybridization can obscure an originally mixed origin.

A few breeds differ by large-effect mutations, which does not by itself imply a different wild species.

Not every fancy breed and not every geographical subspecies of C. livia is sequenced.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.93
data existence: 0.84
discriminating power: 0.84
analysis feasibility: 0.78
data adequacy: 0.72

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: If all domestic pigeon breeds descend from Columba livia (with its geographical sub-species) and not from several wild stocks, then every domestic-breed mitochondrial sequence should fall within the Columba livia cluster: nearer to C. livia sequences than to any other Columba species, and within intraspecific distance of C. livia.

fields.label: Method
fields.value: analysis.py fetches every GenBank mitochondrial record of Columba livia and of all other Columba species, extracts COI and CYTB from the C. livia reference NC_013978.1, and places each record on those genes by best ungapped k-mer-anchored offset (>= 400 bp overlap, >= 80 % identity; complete mitogenomes contribute their annotated genes). Records are domestic if the organism is 'domestica', a /breed qualifier or 'breed:' note is present, or a breed name occurs in the record; breed names are parsed from those fields. For each domestic record and gene, p-distances over >= 300 shared positions give the nearest non-domestic C. livia record and the nearest record of each other Columba species ('Columba sp.' excluded as unidentified). The measured value is the number of domestic records nearer to another species than to C. livia.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Using GenBank mitochondrial records of Columba livia and of all other Columba species, aligned by best ungapped offset to the COI and CYTB genes of the C. livia reference mitogenome NC_013978: every domestic-labelled sequence (organism 'Columba livia domestica', a /breed qualifier, or a breed name in the record) has its nearest non-domestic sequence in C. livia (or in a wild C. livia subspecies), and the maximum p-distance from any domestic sequence to the nearest C. livia sequence is < 2 %. Requires >= 10 domestic-labelled sequences from >= 5 named breeds or 'domestica' records; otherwise inconclusive (underpowered).

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: At least 2 domestic sequences from at least 2 different breeds (or records) are nearer to another Columba species (C. rupestris, C. oenas, C. palumbus, C. guinea, C. leuconota, C. hodgsonii, etc.) than to any C. livia sequence, or exceed 2 % from all C. livia sequences while being within 2 % of another species: refutes (a second wild stock contributes maternal ancestry). Exactly one such sequence: mixed.

fields.label: Unit
fields.value: domestic-labelled Columba livia records whose nearest non-domestic mitochondrial sequence (COI or CYTB) belongs to another Columba species

fields.label: Uncertainty
fields.value: max p-distance from a domestic record to the nearest C. livia record 0.013740458015267175; MIN_SHARED 300 bp

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: Darwin's claim concerns descent of all domestic breeds from one wild species; mitochondrial DNA tests the maternal component of that descent, which is what pre-genomic public data allow. 'Columba livia with its geographical sub-species' is taken as all records with organism Columba livia (any subspecies, including domestica for the domestic set). Columba rupestris, the hill pigeon, is a separate species in modern taxonomy and is treated as an alternative wild stock, although Darwin may have regarded it as a form of C. livia; a domestic sequence nearest to C. rupestris is therefore reported separately in the extra fields as well as counted. Alignment is by best ungapped offset because indels are rare in these coding genes; sequences overlapping the reference gene by < 400 bp are discarded.

fields.label: Datasets
fields.value: NCBI GenBank (nuccore) mitochondrial records of Columba livia (534) and of all other Columba species (645), including the C. livia reference mitogenome NC_013978.1, retrieved through E-utilities

fields.label: Caveats
fields.value:
107 domestic records covering 22 named breeds (English and Indian Fantail, Kassel and other Tumblers, Jacobin, Hungarian Cropper (a pouter), Runt, King, Mondain, German Nun, German Magpie, German Beard, Vienna Highflier, Archangel, Ice pigeon, Lahore, Wroclaw Meat, Shiqi, three Egyptian breeds, 'Lucky') are all nearest to C. livia (mean 0.10 %, maximum 1.37 % p-distance) rather than to any of 20 other Columba species; none approaches C. oenas, C. palumbus, C. guinea or C. leuconota, the species Darwin's contemporaries proposed as alternative stocks. Carriers and Barbs, two breeds Darwin emphasised, are not among the named records.

Discriminating power against Columba rupestris is limited: the hill pigeon is only 1.2-2.6 % from domestic sequences in COI/CYTB, and C. livia and C. rupestris are sister species that hybridise. Every domestic record is nonetheless nearer to C. livia than to C. rupestris (0 of 115 record-gene comparisons the other way). Darwin's own wording ('with its geographical sub-species') would arguably absorb rupestris anyway.

Mitochondrial DNA tests maternal ancestry only; nuclear genomic work (Shapiro et al. 2013 Science; Stringham et al. 2012 Current Biology) also places all breeds within C. livia and is literature, not data used here.

Several GenBank 'Columba janthina' COI barcodes are identical to C. livia sequences and are almost certainly mislabelled; they never became the unique nearest neighbour because an equally close C. livia record always existed, so they did not affect the count.

Non-domestic 'Columba livia' comparators include feral and unlabelled birds, some of which may be domestic in origin; this does not bias the test toward 'supports' because the alternative hypothesis predicts domestic sequences nesting with another species, which would be detected regardless.

Breed labelling was refined twice after inspecting record metadata (parsing 'breed:' notes and isolate names such as '693_Jacobin pigeon'); this changed only how many named breeds were counted (3 -> 22), not the distances or the pre-registered criterion. 'Columba sp.' records were removed from the other-species set after the first run because they are unidentified, not an alternative wild species; no violation existed with them included either.
